entries.topic: Investigation of intermittent Agent support-log uploads
facts: One provided local log from an affected Agent records 22 deferred uploads and one acknowledged success during 13 October 2026, approximately 13:30 to 19:52.
Failures consist of 14 timeouts, five keep-alive closures and three unexpected receive closures.
Agent source enforces 10-second request/read-write timeout; the shared gateway source permits a lock wait up to 15 seconds before archive operations.
Agent upload backoff escalates from one minute to 30 minutes; a manual sealed entry does not prove completed upload.
The Agent was upgraded during the trace and upload failures continued. Available evidence does not prove the same root cause on the second affected Agent.
alternatives: Preserve local pending logs and inspect one other affected Agent for comparison.
Prepare Agent-only change proposal: aligned bounded timeout, serialized upload attempts, safer connection recovery, visible upload status and reliable manual retry.
Investigate gateway contention separately before considering changes to its runtime.
entries.next_action: Await Owner authorization before source changes or deployment; preserve current production operations.
entries.evidence: Owner supplied local support log, 2026-10-13; source files relay-agent/AgentLogUploadBridge.cs and ops/apps-script/agent-log-gateway/Code.gs.

entries.topic: Compare second affected Windows Agent support-log file to first
facts: Owner supplied a second local Agent diagnostic file from another affected workstation. Across 13 October local observations, first Agent has 7,663 lines, 22 GOOGLE_APPS_SCRIPT upload=DEFER (14 timeout, 5 keep-alive connection closed, 3 unexpected receive errors) and one Drive-confirmed upload=PASS; second Agent has 1,983 lines, 20 upload=DEFER (16 timeout, 4 keep-alive closure) and one Drive-confirmed upload=PASS.

Second Agent log spans roughly 13:38 to 20:10 VN; only confirmed Drive upload at 15:18:40, with 15 subsequent failed uploads through 20:09:36. First Agent shows one pass at 13:35:36 and 20 later deferred events through 19:48:57.
Both affected machines ran v130 after local restarts; second logs v125 before changing to v130 at 15:18. Repeated v130 starts on second machine were observed but their cause is not established.

Second Agent manual=SEALED upload=TRY at 20:09:46 followed 20:09:36 timeout by ten seconds and falls inside retry_after 20:39:36 VN; thus that marker is not upload confirmation and existing cooldown can defer manual transmission.

Second Agent performs Firebase refresh PASS and Firestore Confirm poll PASS in same period. This is selective degraded support-log route, not proven total Internet outage or inability to authenticate.

Current Agent source uses request Timeout=10000 ms and ReadWriteTimeout=10000 ms for Gateway HTTP POST, backoff up to 30 minutes and no explicit single-flight gate; gateway source uses waitLock(15000) plus Worker/Drive operations. This is a design mismatch and plausible latency mechanism; shared Apps Script lock delay is not established as actual event cause without execution traces.

Second trace shows three close-together failures at 15:20:43, 15:20:49.136 and 15:20:49.408, motivating verification of concurrent in-flight flush and retry fencing; timing alone does not prove an upload race.
Scope note: original raw user logs remain private and are not committed; only aggregate counts and sanitized aliases are recorded.
alternatives: Measure first, read-only: compare existing Gateway execution durations, completion/Drive receipts and network/proxy behavior for the same time periods; verify local pending count and oldest pending age on both affected agents.

Preferred Owner-reviewed Agent-only fix: serialized log uploads, response-safe timeout and connection handling, bounded backoff/manual retry semantics, unambiguous confirmed-status UI and persisted pending bundles.
Gateway optimization only if measured lock/Worker/Drive execution time implicates backend; no added polling/provider writes or unrelated business modifications.
